actions.title: Unveiling Perceptual Artifacts: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Interpretable AI-Generated Image Detection
actions.task_definition: Section 3.3 defines Authenticity Judgment as real/fake image classification and Perceptual Artifact Detection as prediction of artifact instance regions and one of seven categories. Section 5 studies PAD-only and joint PAD/AJ models, so PAD is a performed auxiliary forensic task, not merely explanatory display.
actions.output_decision_space: A PAD model produces a pixel-level semantic segmentation mask for seven perceptual-artifact categories plus background; the joint model also outputs image-level fake probability. Existing detectors' Grad-CAM/relevance heatmaps and later attention-alignment maps are distinct interpretation outputs and alone would not meet T2.
actions.supervision_and_ground_truth: Section 3.2 describes human polygon masks and artifact categories on fake images. Appendix B.2 describes a segmentation head, multiclass segmentation loss and predicted pixel-level masks at inference. Predictions are compared with held-out annotated artifact regions.
actions.evaluation_evidence: Section 3.3 and appendix A.5 define IoU, pixel precision/recall/F1 and weak instance-level matching against ground-truth regions; section 5, Tables 2-3 report spatial PAD results. Table 2 PAD-only IoU 27.2 and PixF1 42.7; joint multi-task IoU 27.3 and PixF1 42.8, as reported. Interpretation heatmap overlap results are separate and are not the basis of this adjudication.
actions.confidence: high for the spatial task in the retrieved author manuscript; conference-final text equivalence unverified
actions.limitations: The arXiv v1 manuscript predates the inaccessible ICLR final PDF. PAD is artifact-region segmentation on generated images, not a claim of manipulated-region compositing localization.

actions.title: IncreFA: Breaking the Static Wall of Generative Model Attribution
actions.task_definition: Section 3.1 defines source-model attribution with an expanded real, known-generator, and unseen-generator decision space. Section 5.1 evaluates incremental attribution/open-set generator recognition (EP1) and static attribution plus authenticity recognition (EP2).
actions.output_decision_space: The hierarchical formulation first separates real, fake, and unseen (Figure 2); known synthetic images then receive generator/family labels. EP1 starts with a real class and one generator and adds generators; the withheld unknowns are synthetic generators, not real images.
actions.real_image_role: Real COCO images are a labeled class in IABench (section 3.1; section 5.1; Table 2). Their mere presence is not the detection evidence. EP2 explicitly frames and scores real-versus-generated authenticity recognition as a separate metric.
actions.authenticity_evaluation: Section 5.1 defines Auth. Acc. as accuracy distinguishing real from generated images. Table 2 reports IncreFA Auth. Acc. 99.97 and real-class accuracy 99.66. Table 1 also reports Auth. Acc. 99.97 under EP1. The explicit binary metric supports T1 independently of the N+1 real class.
actions.attribution_evaluation: Section 5.1 and Tables 1-2 separately score seen-generator attribution and unknown-synthetic-generator rejection. Table 1 final incremental-task attribution accuracy 78.80 and unseen-generator accuracy 98.93; Table 2 static average attribution accuracy 95.93 and unseen-generator accuracy 98.78. None of these unknown-generator figures is treated as authenticity accuracy.
actions.confidence: high for the explicit authenticity metric and same-work identity; conference-final authorship and exact textual equivalence remain unverified
actions.limitations: The author-deposited v2 includes Yuexuan Tan while the canonical CVPR field has five authors. That known metadata variance is documented, not silently normalized or used to edit publication metadata. The first-pass CVF final PDF remains unread.

resolution.accounting_basis: Both cases were subtracted exactly once when Wave 5B evidence was collected; adjudication applies only T236 and does not reduce the remaining ledger again.
